newsitem.title: UK: LME copper gains ground in late PM, others follow.
newsitem.headline: LME copper gains ground in late PM, others follow.

text.p: Copper prices rose in late inter-office London Metal Exchange (LME) trade on Tuesday, helping to drag some other metal prices higher.

At 1810 GMT three month copper futures were indicated at $1,890/95 a tonne, up from Tuesday's afternoon kerb close of $1,870. London traders said Comex-led buying was behind the move, adding that conditions were thin.
The market now looked poised to test the first upside objective at $1,900, followed by more stiff resistance at around $1,950, traders said.
Cash was indicated at $1/5 over three month values, having moved into a small contango briefly earlier on Tuesday, the first time it had done so since January 1995.
Aluminium was last quoted at $1,420.50/22.50 from $1,416.50.

Although higher copper prices would support aluminium, if LME stocks continued to rise at around Tuesday's rate of 7,400 tonnes for much longer, support at $1,400 was bound to be tested, traders said.
Most other base metals were indicated slightly above their afternoon kerb closing levels, in line with copper's gains.
